description: The checks that run without being asked. A formatter nobody runs, a linter with no rules and a strict flag turned off are all the same failure: a control that exists to be pointed at rather than to catch anything.

gates.title: Prettier Is Configured
gates.rule: A Prettier configuration exists at the root and is not empty. Formatting settled once in a file is formatting nobody argues about in a review.
gates.fix: Add .prettierrc with the project's settings, and .prettierignore for the build output.

gates.title: A format:check Script Exists
gates.rule: The package exposes a script that checks formatting without writing. A formatter with only a write script cannot be a gate, because running it makes the check pass.

gates.title: CI Runs The Formatter Check
gates.rule: The workflow calls format:check. A check that only runs when somebody remembers is a check that runs after the argument rather than before it.
gates.fix: Add the step to .github/workflows/ci.yml on both branches.

gates.title: ESLint Has A Config With Real Rules
gates.rule: A flat config exists and turns on rules beyond the framework's defaults. A config that extends one preset and adds nothing is a linter that agrees with everything.
gates.fix: Write eslint.config.js with the rule set the project actually wants.

gates.title: A lint Script Exists And CI Runs It
gates.rule: The package exposes lint and the workflow calls it. The standard ci.yml runs lint --if-present, which passes silently when the script is missing.
gates.fix: Add the script, and confirm the workflow reaches it.

gates.title: No Silent eslint-disable
gates.rule: Every disable comment names the rule and says why. A bare disable turns off everything on that line for whoever reads it next, and nothing records what it was for.
gates.fix: Name the rule and add the reason, or fix the code the rule is pointing at.

gates.title: TypeScript Runs Strict
gates.rule: strict is on in the tsconfig, with noImplicitAny and strictNullChecks it implies. Strict off is a type checker that agrees with the code rather than checking it.
gates.fix: Turn strict on and work through what it surfaces.

gates.title: No any Escape Hatches In What Changed
gates.rule: The files this run touched carry no explicit any and no ts-ignore. One any at a boundary spreads through everything it returns into.
gates.fix: Type the value, or use unknown and narrow it.

gates.title: The Type Check Runs In CI
gates.rule: The workflow runs tsc --noEmit. A build that transpiles without checking types ships type errors, because most bundlers do not check at all.
gates.fix: Add a typecheck script and call it from ci.yml.

gates.title: One Lockfile, Committed
gates.rule: Exactly one lockfile exists and it is tracked. Two lockfiles mean two dependency trees and whichever tool ran last wins; none means CI resolves versions the developer never saw.
gates.fix: Delete the lockfiles for package managers this project does not use, and commit the one that is left.

gates.title: The Node Version Is Pinned And CI Agrees
gates.rule: engines.node names a version and the workflow's setup-node matches it. A project that builds locally on one major and in CI on another fails in exactly the places the two differ.
gates.fix: Set engines.node, and set node-version in ci.yml to the same major.

gates.title: Editor Configuration Is Ignored, Not Committed
gates.rule: gitignore covers .idea, .vscode, *.iml and the rest, and none of them is tracked. Editor settings are personal and belong in the machine, not handed to whoever clones next.
gates.fix: Add the entries and git rm --cached anything already tracked.
